parsed.rationale: Two computed properties in the same `Wallpaper` package — `ProcessInfo.ThermalState.description` in the sample-app's `DebugHUD.swift` (line 237) and `PerformanceControls.thermalStateLabel` in `PerformanceControls.swift` (line 152) — share near-identical logic (Jaccard 0.75) for converting a `ProcessInfo.ThermalState` value to a human-readable string. The canonical home for this logic is a single `extension ProcessInfo.ThermalState` in the production `Wallpaper` source tree (e.g., a new file under `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/DebugUI/`), which both the sample app and `PerformanceControls` can then consume. Because one member carries `is_sample_app: true`, the duplication is partly explained by the sample app copying production logic, but the production copy in `PerformanceControls.swift` is itself a local helper rather than a proper extension, so consolidation is still warranted.
